title: POC quantization healthcheck — throughput regression review
summary: Weekly POC sync to investigate a throughput regression observed with INT8 on long-context jobs. Reviewed FP8 vs INT8 perf, sample-level quality deltas, KV cache behavior, and next steps for focused benchmarking and a small dedicated fallback canary.
topics: quality-impact on summarization and long context
KV cache warming and eviction patterns
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-29 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Tran (Redwood AE), Miguel Alvarez (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Canyon Analytics - ML Eng), Priya Rao (Canyon - ML Ops), Samir Patel (Canyon - Infra), Jill Morris (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Investigated throughput regression when switching to INT8 for long-context summarization workload. FP8 had higher tail latency but INT8 showed unexpected p99 spikes and occasional hallucinations on 8k+ contexts. Action items agreed: more deterministic perf runs, curated failure set from customer, and explore dedicated canary fallback + KV cache tuning.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie: alright good afternoon everyone thanks for joining our weekly POC health check. is this still a good time?
[00:07] Alex: yeah good here, thanks Sophie. we've got a couple of engineers on the call who saw the regression yesterday.
[00:12] Sophie: cool, quick agenda — recap results since last week, dig into the regression traces, agree on targeted perf runs and next steps. Miguel will lead the perf bits.
[00:22] Miguel: yep hi all, I'll share my screen after the quick walkthrough, but to tee up, we saw INT8 token throughput drop on the 8k jobs — p50 roughly same but p99 jumped from ~120ms to 640ms, tokens/sec down ~30%.
[00:36] Priya: that matches what we saw on our side. Some jobs timed out in our internal queue which is why some summaries got cut off.
[00:43] Sophie: ok can you describe the config — are you using KV cache enabled? batching settings?
[00:48] Samir: default caching yes, KV cache on, batch size 16, but we had autoscale add nodes so there may have been cold V P C links while nodes booted.
[00:57] Miguel: two quick notes: 1) INT8 kernel path is faster on average but less tolerant to long KV sequences if the cache isn't warmed; 2) FP8 kept more graceful tails for our test samples so p99 retained.
[01:12] Alex: I remember last week FP8 had slightly worse nominal cost but better tail — is that what you mean?
[01:16] Miguel: exactly — FP8 was ~510 tokens/sec on our 8k bench, INT8 dropped to ~370 in one run, but in other runs INT8 hit 720 tokens/sec. variability looks correlated with cache hit rate and sequence length distribution.
[01:33] Jill: variability is the thing. our SLA is p99 < 700ms for the user flow. these spikes are concerning.
[01:40] Sophie: understoood. let's jump into a trace Miguel attached — the perf sheet link is in the notes (link: https://redwood.test/benchmarks/quant-poc-0429).
[01:51] Miguel: reading from the trace here — at 00:12 the request experienced a KV miss cascade, then there was a small GPU O O M on the worker which caused a backlog. transcription note: GPU oom sometimes shows as "GPU uh mm" in our logs.
[02:05] Samir: we saw node restarts in our cluster at the same timestamps, likely caused by ephemeral autoscaling; could be infra side.
[02:12] Priya: we did push a change to our autoscaler yesterday to be more aggressive for burst traffic, maybe that interacted poorly.
[02:18] Sophie: ok so possible contributing factors: autoscaler and cold caches. Any evidence this is purely infra and not quantization?
[02:26] Miguel: not purely, we ran controlled single-node runs: with fully-warmed KV cache INT8 still had a small number of hallucination regressions on the summarization tests for very long docs. quality-wise FP8 slightly better on ROUGE and human checks for the 12k+ token set.
[02:44] Alex: by hallucinations you mean factual errors or tokenization artifacts?
[02:48] Miguel: factual drift and occasionally repeated phrases — seems like precision loss in some attention computations under INT8 for long context. but it's limited to ~2-3% of samples.
[02:58] Priya: that 2-3% is user impacting though; we have a safety bar of <1% on production.
[03:04] Sophie: noted. let's prioritize: get deterministic perf runs, get a labeled failure set, and explore a fallback canary on dedicated capacity.
[03:12] Miguel: proposed runs: single-client deterministic runs with seeded RNG, three sequence lengths (2k, 8k, 16k), both INT8 and FP8, KV cache cold/warm. capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and memory usage.
[03:26] Alex: we can provide the long-doc examples — I'll pull a set of 50 that failed.
[03:30] Sophie: perfect. timeline?
[03:33] Miguel: I can run the deterministic suite and upload CSVs by Monday 2026-05-03 if we start tonight.
[03:39] Alex: Monday works.
[03:41] Jill: on the fallback canary, what's the approach?
[03:44] Miguel: plan is a small dedicated pool with pinned FP8 model variant that automatically receives 10% of the traffic for the summarization route — if regression detected, route rises. Redwood provides canary routing in the console.
[03:56] Samir: cost concern — dedicated pool will be more expensive. we'll need pricing delta.
[03:59] Sophie: I'll share an updated pricing sheet; estimate 18% uplift for the small dedicated burst pool but with more predictable tails.
[04:07] Priya: also want to confirm security controls — if we move to dedicated, how's KMS integration and audit logs?
[04:13] Miguel: dedicated and Private both support customer-managed KMS, SAML SSO, and we can produce audit logs per request (we do sample-based audit retention by default, full retention is an add-on).
[04:24] Alex: can you provide SOC2 artifact and KMS integration docs?
[04:27] Sophie: yes, I'll drop the security pack and the compliance deck after the call. link placeholder: /security-pack.
[04:34] Miguel: back to perf, one nuance — our INT8 kernels are sensitive to quantization calibration; some of the 8k samples have rare tokens that shift dynamic range. we can try a per-shard calibration or mixed-precision for the attention matrices.
[04:49] Alex: is that something we can toggle without re-training?
[04:51] Miguel: yes, it's a serving-time config and quant profile switch — not retraining. there are tradeoffs: mixed path reduces speed but preserves quality.
[04:59] Priya: could we try INT8 with attention in FP16? that hybrid might be close to FP8 quality but keep some INT8 speed wins.
[05:05] Miguel: exactly, we call that attention hybrid. we'll include that in the runs.
[05:09] Sophie: great. any blockers for running the deterministic suite?
[05:12] Alex: we need instructions for reproducing the KV warm/cold states reliably.
[05:16] Miguel: will write a small harness and push to the shared drive with steps: pre-warm by sending X prefix requests, then run the target batch. I'll also instrument cache hit rates.
[05:27] Alex: perfect.
[05:29] Sophie: ok security aside, let's talk about monitoring: we need alerting on p99 and hallucination rate. can Redwood surface a quality metric?
[05:38] Miguel: yes, Redwood Optimize can ingest eval sets and surface regressions. For now we'll push metrics into the console and set a p99 alert, and a custom webhook for our hallucination flag.
[05:49] Priya: we'll need the webhook endpoint and a sample payload.
[05:52] Miguel: will include sample payloads in the harness repo.
[05:56] Jill: quick Q — any competitor noise? we looked at a managed offering from Anthropic that claims better tail on long-context, but we couldn't run our exact workload.
[06:07] Sophie: noted, we'll stick to empirical runs.
[06:10] Miguel: one other data point: FP8 latency had a few high memory pressure events, but it didn't trigger timeouts. INT8 was more susceptible to token-level precision drops.
[06:22] Alex: curious if quantization interacts with prompt-engineering. we saw fewer failures when the prompt had more anchoring context.
[06:28] Miguel: yeah anchoring helps; we'll include that axis as well.
[06:31] Sophie: ok action recaps — Miguel will run deterministic suite and share CSVs; Alex will deliver failure examples; Sophie will send pricing + security docs.
[06:41] Samir: can we also get a quick checklist for the dedicated canary setup so infra can provision?
[06:45] Miguel: yes short runbook: small N GPU pool, model pin to FP8, route 10% with weighted policy and automatic rollback threshold at 1.5x baseline error. I'll write it up.
[06:57] Alex: timeline for the canary?
[06:59] Sophie: propose we stand it up Tuesday 2026-05-05 after we've seen the deterministic run results; start at 10% traffic for 48 hours.
[07:07] Priya: sounds good.
[07:10] Jill: any other research-level asks?
[07:12] Miguel: maybe one: run mixed precision attention for 8k+ only and capture quality deltas.
[07:18] Alex: we'll prioritize that.
[07:20] Sophie: ok cool. before we close any gotchas?
[07:23] Priya: just one note — on our side we need SAML service provider metadata for the dedicated cluster earlier than the canary day so we can validate.
[07:31] Sophie: I'll ask security to ship that tonight.
[07:34] Miguel: also a small note on instrumentation: please ensure trace IDs are passed through so we can correlate Redwood logs with your infra logs.
[07:42] Samir: will do.
[07:44] Sophie: ok great, recap next steps coming in calendar and I'll attach the benchmark link and the security pack. thanks everyone.
[07:51] Alex: thanks folks, bye.
[07:53] Jill: bye.

End of call.
action_items: Miguel Alvarez - run deterministic perf suite (2k / 8k / 16k) for INT8, FP8, and hybrid attention, include cold/warm KV runs, upload CSVs — due 2026-05-03
Alex Chen - provide 50 long-document examples that exhibited hallucination/regression under INT8, mark ground-truth and severity — due 2026-05-01
Sophie Tran - share updated pricing delta for small dedicated fallback and security pack (SOC2, KMS integration, SAML metadata) — due 2026-04-30
Miguel Alvarez - write dedicated canary runbook and rollback thresholds doc — due 2026-05-04
next_steps: Start deterministic perf runs (Miguel) and review results on Mon 2026-05-03 call
Stand up small dedicated FP8 canary (10% traffic) on Tue 2026-05-05 if deterministic results justify
Customer to label failure set and prioritize top 10 for triage
